title: DFS in Reykjavík: Find Any Route!
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) crawl through Reykjavík’s street-like graph to reach a target node. The visualization highlights how DFS explores deep paths first, then backtracks to uncover an escape route.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ **DFS in Reykjavík (Miðborg)!** ✨🧭

Depth-First Search (DFS) explores a path by going **as deep as possible** before backtracking. In graph terms, each intersection is a **node** and each street segment is an **edge**—DFS uses a **stack/recursion** to traverse neighbors, marking visited nodes to avoid cycles.

🌍 Real-world twist: when we model street maps as a graph (like Reykjavík’s central grid), DFS can quickly dive into one corridor, then retreat and try alternate branches when the path dead-ends. That “go deep, then backtrack” behavior is the hallmark of DFS—simple, fast per step, and perfect for teaching traversal mechanics.

fb_caption:
🌍🚦 **DFS on real street-map graphs from Reykjavík!**

Depth-First Search (DFS) is a graph search algorithm that goes deep into one branch before backtracking, using visited tracking to prevent loops. In this visualization, intersections are nodes and road segments are edges—then DFS “walks” the map until it finds the target.
